standard-dialogue-before-the-knight-s-sw.player: What is that cape you're wearing?

standard-dialogue-before-the-knight-s-sw.npc: It's a Skillcape of Smithing. It shows that I'm a master blacksmith, but that's only to be expected - after all, my ancestors were the greatest blacksmiths in dwarven history.
If you ever achieve level 99 Smithing you'll be able to wear a cape like this, and receive more experience when smelting gold ore.

options.text: Can you make me another of Sir Vyvin's swords?

steps.player: Can you make me another of Sir Vyvin's swords?

steps.npc: You want that knight's sword again? I suppose you brought me a lovely pie, so I don't mind. I'll need a blurite ore and two iron bars, like before.

steps.text: If the player has a blurite ore and two iron bars:
Thurgo makes you another sword
Blurite sword
If the player does not have all the required materials:

steps.player: Okay, I'll go and find that.

options.text: Would you like a redberry pie?

steps.player: Would you like a redberry pie?

steps.text: You see Thurgo's eyes light up.
Normal dialogue:

steps.npc: I'd never say no to a redberry pie! We Imcando dwarves love them - they're GREAT!

steps.text: You hand over the pie. Thurgo eats the pie. Thurgo pats his stomach.

steps.npc: By Guthix! THAT was good pie! Anyone who makes pie like THAT has got to be alright!

steps.text: Unknown condition:

steps.npc: Another? By Guthix, you are generous! I like you!

steps.text: You watch Thurgo greedily gobble down the pie.

steps.npc: BUUUUUUUUUUUUUURP Mmmmm... I could eat redberry pies all day!

options.text: What is that cape you're wearing?
options.condition: If the player does not have 99 Smithing:

steps.player: What is that cape you're wearing?

steps.npc: It's a Skillcape of Smithing. It shows that I'm a master blacksmith, but that's only to be expected - after all, my ancestors were the greatest blacksmiths in dwarven history.
If you ever achieve level 99 Smithing you'll be able to wear a cape like this, and receive more experience when smelting gold ore.
What do you need, human?

steps.player: Now that I am so skilled at Smithing, can I buy a Skillcape of Smithing from you?

steps.npc: I reckon so; we master smiths must stick together! I'll give it to you for just 99000 coins.
Too much money? A smith of your calibre should be able to make that amount in an hour!

steps.text: If the player does not have at least 99,000 coins:
If the player has at least 99,000 coins but not enough inventory space:

steps.npc: All Skillcapes come with a free hood. It's part of a deal: buy one get one free, you know. So you'll need to free up some inventory space before I can sell you one.

steps.text: If the player has at least 99,000 coins and enough inventory space:
a Smithing cape and hood

steps.npc: Excellent! Wear that cape with pride my friend.

options.condition: If the player has talked to Ramarno after completing Below Ice Mountain:

steps.npc: I very much doubt that [player name]. I'm the last Imcando dwarf left in Gielinor.

steps.player: No it's true. I was accidentally helping some grave robbers unearth some treasure below Ice Mountain. Long story short, it turned out to be the ruins of Camdozaal.

steps.npc: Camdozaal?
I don't believe me ears! Tell me what else you know!

steps.player: Well there's not much left there really. It's just a ruin.
But there's a lone Imcando dwarf keeping it alive. His name is Ramarno.

steps.npc: Ramarno...

steps.player: He's managed to keep the city going all these years, even with his lack of vision.

steps.npc: Thank you for bringing me this news [player name]. I'll need to make some time to see the city with my own eyes.

steps.player: Can you help me make another crowbar?

steps.npc: I can indeed. We'll need a hammer, a steel bar, and of course, a redberry pie.

steps.player: I don't have all of that I'm afraid...

steps.npc: Well, come back when you do.

standard-dialogue-using-imcandoria-s-fal.player: What do you make of this, Thurgo?

standard-dialogue-using-imcandoria-s-fal.npc: Hmph, who wrote this text? It seems new.
Nevermind! If you ever plan on going back to this island, I'll happily come along.

standard-dialogue-using-imcandoria-s-fal.player: So you believe it could possibly lead to the ancient ruins of your race?

standard-dialogue-using-imcandoria-s-fal.npc: I'll believe it when I see it... Now begone, I've got things to do.

standard-dialogue-using-imcandoria-s-fal.player: Alright, Thurgo. I'll see you later.

delivering-a-letter-from-the-wise-old-ma.player: The Wise Old Man says he's got the information you wanted. Here's his message.

delivering-a-letter-from-the-wise-old-ma.npc: Ooh, thanks. I've been hoping he'd send me that information soon, although I wouldn't mind if he'd send me a pie instead!

delivering-a-letter-from-the-wise-old-ma.text: If the player has a full inventory upon collecting a reward:

steps.npc: I'd give you a reward, but you don't seem to have any space for it. Come back when you do.

delivering-a-letter-from-the-wise-old-ma.text: If the player has at least one free space:

steps.text: If the player is rewarded with herbs:
Thurgo gives you some banknotes that can be exchanged for herbs.
an assortment of herbs

steps.npc: Some guy died down in the hole just north of my house, and he dropped these herbs. Here, take them.

steps.text: If the player is rewarded with coins:
Thurgo gives you some coins.
some coins

steps.npc: Here's some cash for your time.

steps.text: If the player is rewarded with gems:
a gem
Thurgo gives you an Uncut emerald!

steps.npc: I found this while I was mining. Hope you like it.

steps.text: If the player is rewarded with seeds:
If the player is rewarded with runes:
Thurgo gives you some runes.
an assortment of runes

steps.npc: Magic isn't really my thing. Here, take these.
